rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṭrus leads his Muslim companion through both gardens, showing them off and boasting of the wealth he owns beyond the companion’s means.
rows.anchor: قطروس أخذ بيد أخيه المسلم يطوف به في الجنتين ويريه ما فيهما ويعجبه منهما ويفاخره بما ملك من المال دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular ‘his garden’ means his own property, his worldly garden alone; he has no share in the Garden promised to believers, and neither garden individually is meant.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه لا نصيب له في الجنة التي وعد المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wrongs himself by admiring and boasting of his gift, being ungrateful to God, and exposing himself to divine anger; this is the worst injustice.
rows.anchor: وهو معجب بما أوتي مفتخر به كافر لنعمة ربه ، معرض بذلك نفسه لسخط الله ، وهو أفحش الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His professed doubt that the garden will endure reflects long hopes, greed, prolonged heedlessness, delusion by respite, and neglect of consequences.
rows.anchor: إخباره عن نفسه بالشك في بيدودة جنته : لطول أمله واستيلاء الحرص عليه وتمادي غفلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even wealthy Muslims who do not say this aloud have lives whose outward state proclaims the same assumption.
rows.anchor: فإن ألسنة أحوالهم ناطقة به منادية عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His oath that he would find something better if returned to God is hypothetical wishful thinking based on his companion’s premise.
rows.anchor: إقسام منه على أنه إن رد إلى ربه على سبيل الفرض والتقدير وكما يزعم صاحبه ليجدن في الآخرة خيرا من جنته في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presumes God’s favor and his own standing, treating the gardens as proof of deserved merit that will accompany him wherever he goes.
rows.anchor: وأن معه هذا الاستحقاق أينما توجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘better than them’ is also read, referring back to the two gardens.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( خيرا منهما ) ردا على الجنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munqalaban means a return or outcome, and is accusative as specification: the afterlife outcome is better than this garden’s because it lasts while this one perishes.
rows.anchor: مرجعا وعاقبة . وانتصابه على التمييز ، أي : منقلب تلك ، خير من منقلب هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating the addressee from dust means creating his origin, since creating the origin causes his own creation and is therefore attributed to him.
rows.anchor: أي خلق أصلك ، لأن خلق أصله سبب في خلقه ، فكان خلقه خلقا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwāka means proportioned and completed him as a male human who reached adulthood.
rows.anchor: عدلك وكملك إنسانا ذكرا بالغا مبلغ الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His doubt about resurrection makes him an unbeliever in God and a denier of His blessings, just as denying a Messenger makes one an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: جعله كافرا بالله جاحدا لأنعمه لشكه في البعث ، كما يكون المكذب بالرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Was encompassed’ signifies that the garden was destroyed; the image comes from an enemy surrounding and mastering someone, then extends to any destruction.
rows.anchor: به عبارة عن إهلاكه . وأصله من أحاط به العدو ؛ لأنه إذا أحاط به فقد ملكه واستولى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning the palms over is a metaphor for regret and grief, as a regretful person turns the hands palm up and down; the wording uses ‘over’ because regret takes that construction.
rows.anchor: كناية عن الندم والتحسر ، لأن النادم يقلب كفيه ظهرا لبطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret concerns what he spent building the garden.
rows.anchor: فأصبح يندم { على ما أنفق فيها } أي أنفق في عمارتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trellises of its vines fell to the ground, with the vines falling over them.
rows.anchor: يعني أن كرومها المعرشة سقطت عروشها على الأرض ، وسقطت فوقها الكروم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported explanation says God sent fire that consumed the garden.
rows.anchor: قيل : أرسل الله عليها نارا فأكلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering his brother’s admonition, the owner realizes his associationism and rebellion brought the disaster and wishes he had not associated anything with God.
rows.anchor: تذكر موعظة أخيه فعلم أنه أتى من جهة شركه وطغيانه ، فتمنى لو لم يكن مشركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish may also be repentance for associationism, regret for his conduct, and entry into faith.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون توبة من الشرك ، وندما على ما كان منه ، ودخولا في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ‘they help him’ is read with either masculine or feminine agreement, with agreement by sense rather than grammatical form; compare the group that fights and ‘they see them’.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ولم يكن ) بالياء والتاء ، وحمل { ينصرونه } على المعنى دون اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They could help him apart from God’ means they had the capacity to help; only God could aid him, but He withheld aid because the man deserved abandonment.
rows.anchor: قلت : معناه يقدرون على نصرته من دون الله ، أي : هو وحده القادر على نصرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He could not use his own strength to protect himself from God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: وما كان منتصرا } وما كان ممتنعا بقوته عن انتقام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, al-wilāya means aid or taking charge; with kasra, it means sovereignty and dominion, and both readings are reported.
rows.anchor: بالفتح النصرة والتولي ، وبالكسر السلطان والملك ، وقد قرىء بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that occasion, aid belongs to God alone; no one else owns or can provide it, confirming the preceding statement that no faction could help.
rows.anchor: في ذلك المقام وتلك الحال النصرة لله وحده ، لا يملكها غيره ، ولا يستطيعها أحد سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means sovereignty and dominion belong to God, whom none can overcome or evade.
rows.anchor: أو : هنالك السلطان والملك لله لا يغلب ولا يمتنع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, in severe distress everyone turns to God and believes; the ruined owner’s cry of regret was forced by calamity and panic, and without it he would not have said it.
rows.anchor: يعني أن قوله { ويقول ياليتنى لم أشرك بربى أحدا } ( الكهف : 42 ) كلمة ألجيء إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God supports His believing allies against disbelievers, avenges them, and comforts them; destroying the disbeliever vindicated his believing brother and fulfilled the latter’s prediction.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : هالك الولاية لله ينصر فيها أولياءه المؤمنين على الكفرة وينتقم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Best in reward and outcome’ in this interpretation describes God’s believing allies.
rows.anchor: ويعضده قوله { خير ثوابا وخير عقبا } أي لأوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘there’ points to the afterlife, as in the declaration that sovereignty belongs to God on that Day.
rows.anchor: وقيل { هنالك } إشارة إلى الآخرة أي في تلك الدار الولاية لله ، كقوله { لمن الملك اليوم } ( غافر : 16 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq is read nominative as an adjective of al-wilāya or God; ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reads it accusative for emphasis, a polished and eloquent reading.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( الحق ) بالرفع والجر صفة للولاية والله . وقرأ عمرو بن عبيد بالنصب على التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author praises ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd as among the most eloquent and sincere people.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة حسنة فصيحة ، وكان عمرو بن عبيد من أفصح الناس وأنصحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUquban is read with a ḍamma or sukūn, or as ʿuqbā; all forms mean the final outcome.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( عقبا ) بضم القاف وسكونها ، وعقبى على فعلى ، وكلها بمعنى العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring righteous deeds are good acts whose fruits remain for a person while worldly desires and benefits perish.
rows.anchor: أعمال الخير التي تبقى ثمرتها للإنسان وتفنى عنه كل ما تطمح إليه نفسه من حظوظ الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the enduring deeds as the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as saying glorification, praise, that none is god but God, and God is greatest.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إلاه إلا الله والله أكبر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the phrase includes everything done seeking God’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : كل ما أريد به وجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are better in reward and hope: their doer hopes for God’s reward in this world and receives it in the next.
rows.anchor: أي ما يتعلق بها من الثواب وما يتعلق بها من الأمل ؛ لأن صاحبها يأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are read as being moved or moving through the air, or as being taken away and made into scattered dust.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( تسير ) من سيرت ، ونسير من سيرنا ( وتسير ) من سارت ، أي : تسير في الجو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading of ‘you see the earth’ presents it as exposed, stripped of what had covered it.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وترى الأرض ) على البناء للمفعول { بارزة } ليس عليها ما يسيرها مما كان عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We gathered them’ means bringing them together at the place of standing.
rows.anchor: وجمعناهم إلى الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We left none’ is read with either first-person nūn or third-person yāʾ; ghādara and aghdara both mean to leave, as do related words for betrayal and a pool left by a flood.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فلم نغادر ) بالنون والياء ، يقال : غادره وأغدره إذا تركه . ومنه الغدر . ترك الوفاء . والغدير : ما غادره السيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lined-up presentation resembles troops before a ruler: they are all exposed, each person visible without anyone hiding another.
rows.anchor: وشبهت حالهم بحال الجند المعروضين على السلطان { صفا } مصطفين ظاهرين ، يرى جماعتهم كما يرى كل واحد لا يحجب أحد أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You have come to Us’ is what God says to them; this implied saying governs the accusative ‘on the day,’ though an implied ‘remember’ is another parse.
rows.anchor: أي قلنا لهم : لقد جئتمونا . وهذا المضمر هو عامل النصب في يوم نسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are resurrected as God first created them; another view says they arrive naked and without possessions, as when first created.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لقد بعثناكم كما أنشأناكم { أول مرة } وقيل : جئتمونا عراة لا شيء معكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense ‘We gathered them’ indicates that gathering precedes the mountains’ movement and the earth’s emergence, so they witness those great terrors.
rows.anchor: قلت : للدلالة على أن حشرهم قبل التسيير وقبل البروز ، ليعاينوا تلك الأهوال العظائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised appointment is the time for fulfilling what the prophets foretold about resurrection and rising.
rows.anchor: موعدا } وقتا لإنجاز ما وعدتم على ألسنة الأنبياء من البعث والنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘Book’ is a generic collective referring to the sheets of deeds.
rows.anchor: للجنس وهو صحف الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call specifically for the ruin that has overtaken them, singling it out from all ruin.
rows.anchor: يا ويلتنا } ينادون هلكتهم التي هلكوها خاصة من بين الهلكات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Small or great’ is an exhaustive idiom: nothing is left out because everything is either small or great; alternatively, it refers to their minor and major sins.
rows.anchor: لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة } هنة صغيرة ولا كبيرة ، وهي عبارة عن الإحاطة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says that since they avoided no major sins, their minor sins were recorded too, amounting to close scrutiny.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لم يجتنبوا الكبائر فكتبت عليهم الصغائر وهي المناقشة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies a smile as the minor sin and a loud laugh as the major one.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : الصغيرة التبسم ، والكبيرة القهقهة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identifies touching as the minor sin and adultery as the major one.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : الصغيرة المسيس ، والكبيرة الزنا

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl would say that people lamented over minor sins before even reaching the major sins.
rows.anchor: وعن الفضيل : كان إذا قرأها قال : ضجوا والله من الصغائر قبل الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To enumerate it is to record and delimit it precisely; what they did is present either in the records or as its ready recompense.
rows.anchor: إلا أحصاها } إلا ضبطها وحصرها { ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا } في الصحف عتيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wrongs no one by recording uncommitted deeds, increasing deserved punishment, or punishing without a crime; this rejects the claim that He punishes polytheist children for their fathers’ sins.
rows.anchor: ولا يظلم ربك أحدا } فيكتب عليه ما لم يعمل . أو يزيد في عقاب المستحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical ‘he was one of the jinn’ explains why Satan did not prostrate after being excepted from those who did.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف جار مجرى التقليل بعد استثناء إبليس من الساجدين ، كأن قائلا قال : ما له لم يسجد ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His being a jinn explains his disobedience: unlike jinn and humans, angels are absolutely protected from such acts; this guards belief in their sinlessness, as 21:27 says.
rows.anchor: جعل كونه من الجن سببا في فسقه ؛ لأنه لو كان ملكا كسائر من سجد لآدم لم يفسق عن أمر الله ، لأن الملائكة معصومون البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the contrary claim that Satan was an angel and chief who sinned, was cursed and transformed into a devil, and says this was falsely pinned on Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: فما أبعد البون بين ما تعمده الله ، وبين قول من ضاده وزعم أنه كان ملكا ورئيسا ، فعصى ، فلعن ومسخ شيطانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasaqa ʿan amri rabbihi means he departed from his Lord’s order to prostrate.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { فسق * عن أمر ربه } خرج عما أمره به ربه من السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic phrase uses fāsiq to mean straying from a course; an alternative says he became sinful and unbelieving because of the command to prostrate.
rows.anchor: فواسقا عن قصدها جوائرا ; أو صار فاسقا كافرا بسبب أمر ربه الذي هو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza in ‘Would you then take him’ expresses rejection and astonishment at taking Satan and his descendants as allies instead of God after what he did.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار والتعجيب ، كأنه قيل : أعقيب ما وجد منه تتخذونه { وذريته أولياء من دونى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing God with Satan is a bad exchange: it means obeying Satan instead of obeying God.
rows.anchor: بئس البدل من الله إبليس لمن استبدله ، فأطاعه بدل طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s not making them witnesses to creation denies their divinity: they could be partners in worship only if they were partners in Godhood and helped create the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: يعني : أنكم اتخذتموهم شركاء لي في العبادة ، وإنما كانوا يكونون شركاء فيها لو كانوا شركاء في الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Nor the creation of themselves’ means God did not let any of them witness the creation of another, as in ‘do not kill yourselves.’
rows.anchor: أي ول ا أشهدت بعضهم خلق بعض كقوله : { ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم } ( النساء : 29 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them ‘misleaders’ instead of using a pronoun disparages their leading others astray; since they did not help in creation, people should not make them partners in worship.
rows.anchor: فوضع المضلين موضع الضمير ذما لهم بالإضلال ، فإذا لم يكونوا عضدا لي في الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading ‘We did not make them witnesses’ uses the first-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ما أشهدناهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the tāʾ in ‘I was not taking,’ the address is to the Messenger: he could not properly seek their support or rely on them.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وما كنت ) بالفتح : الخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، والمعنى : وما صح لك الاعتضاد بهم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reads muttakhidhan with nunation, following the original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه : ( وما كنت متخذا المضلين ) بالتنوين على الأصل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ʿaḍdan with a still ḍād and transfers its ḍamma to the ʿayn; other variants include several vowel patterns, including plural forms meaning helpers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( عضدا ) بسكون الضاد ، ونقل ضمتها إلى العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ‘he says’ is read with either yāʾ or nūn.
rows.anchor: بالياء والنون . وإضافة الشركاء إليه على زعمهم : توبيخا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them ‘partners’ is a rebuke that adopts their own claim; the partners meant are the jinn.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الشركاء إليه على زعمهم : توبيخا لهم وأراد الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mūbiq means a place of ruin, from verbs meaning to perish or cause to perish; alternatively it is a noun for a shared valley in Hell, a place of ruin and severe torment.
rows.anchor: الموبق : المهلك ، من وبق يبق وبوقا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says al-mūbiq means enmity so intense that it is ruin, illustrated by a poetic warning against love becoming excessive or hatred destructive.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن { موبقا } عداوة . والمعنى : عداوة هي في شدتها هلاك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says al-bayn means connection: the partners’ worldly connection becomes ruin for them at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : البين الوصل أي : وجعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا هلاكا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the partners are angels, ʿUzayr, Jesus, and Mary, with al-mūbiq meaning the distant barrier separating their places in Hell and the highest gardens.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد الملائكة وعزيرا وعيسى ومريم ، وبالموبق : البرزخ البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ẓannū means they became certain; muwāqiʿūhā means they will encounter and fall into the Fire.
rows.anchor: فظنوا } فأيقنوا { مواقعوها } مخالطوها واقعون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṣrifan means a way of turning aside; the author cites a poetic line addressed to Zuhayr as a witness.
rows.anchor: مصرفا } معدلا . قال : أزهير هل عن شيبة من مصرف ;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are more argumentative than any other thing capable of argument, taken one by one; their dispute is contention and false wrangling, with jadalan in the accusative as specification.
rows.anchor: أكثر الأشياء التي يتأتى منها الجدل إن فصلتها واحدا بعد واحد ، خصومة ومماراة بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is like ‘then he is a clear disputant.’
rows.anchor: ونحوه : { فإذا هو خصيم مبين } ( النحل : 4 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first an is accusative and the second nominative; an omitted noun, ‘faith,’ is understood before the first. Nothing prevented faith and seeking forgiveness except waiting for the fate of earlier peoples or the punishment.
rows.anchor: الأولى نصب . والثانية رفع ، وقبلها مضاف محذوف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent of earlier peoples means their destruction, while the punishment is the punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: سنة الاولين } وهي الإهلاك { أو } انتظار أن { يأتيهم العذاب } يعني عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qubulan is read as visibly, as a plural meaning kinds, or with two fatḥas meaning face-to-face or forthcoming.
rows.anchor: قبلا } عيانا . وقرىء : ( قبلا ) أنواعا : جمع قبيل . و ( قبلا ) ، بفتحتين : مستقبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yudḥiḍū means to remove or invalidate, from idḥāḍ al-qadam, making a foot slip from its foothold.
rows.anchor: {ليدحضوا } ليزيلوا ويبطلوا ، من إدحاض القدم وهو إزلاقها وإزالتها عن موطئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘what they were warned,’ mā may be a relative pronoun with an omitted referent, meaning the punishment they were warned about, or a verbal noun meaning their warning.
rows.anchor: { وما أنذروا } يجوز أن تكون { ما } موصولة ، ويكون الراجع من الصلة محذوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading huzʾan with a still hamza means they made the signs objects of mockery.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( هزأ ) ، بالسكون ، أي : اتخذوها موضع استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their false argument to the messengers was that they were only humans like them and that God would have sent angels if He wished.
rows.anchor: وجدالهم : قولهم للرسل : { ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا * ولو شاء الله لانزل ملائكة } ( المؤمنون : 24 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminders are the Qurʾān, explaining why the pronoun for it is masculine; turning away means neither remembering when reminded nor reflecting.
rows.anchor: بأ ايات ربه } بالقرآن ، ولذلك رجع إليها الضمير مذكرا في قوله : { أن يفقهوه } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forget the consequence of their prior disbelief and sins, failing to consider that wrongdoer and doer of good must receive recompense.
rows.anchor: ونسِي } عاقبة { ما قدمت يداه } من الكفر والمعاصي ، غير مفكر فيها ولا ناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away and forgetfulness are explained by sealed hearts; the discourse shifts from singular to plural, following the literal and collective senses of ‘whoever.’
rows.anchor: ثم علل إعراضهم ونسيانهم بأنهم مطبوع على قلوبهم ، وجمع بعد الإفراد حملا على لفظ من ومعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their never attaining guidance is presented as practically impossible because of their fixed resolve; ‘ever’ covers the whole period of moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: فلن يهتدوا } فلا يكون منهم اهتداء البتة ، كأنه محال منهم لشدة تصميمهم { أبدا } مدة التكليف كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhan marks consequence and response: the Messenger’s invitation, which should cause guidance, instead confirms its absence; alternatively, it answers his possible question about continuing to invite them in hope of their conversion.
rows.anchor: و { إذا } جزاء وجواب ، فدل على انتفاء اهتدائهم لدعوة الرسول ، بمعنى أنهم جعلوا ما يجب أن يكون سبب وجود الاهتداء سببا في انتفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghafūr means abundantly forgiving, and dhū al-raḥma means characterized by mercy.
rows.anchor: {الغفور } البليغ المغفرة { ذو الرحمة } الموصوف بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forbearance is shown by delaying punishment for the people of Mecca despite their extreme hostility to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ثم استشهد على ذلك بترك مؤاخذة أهل مكة عاجلا من غير إمهال مع إفراطهم في عداوة رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appointed time is the day of Badr, and they will find no rescue or refuge from it.
rows.anchor: { بل لهم موعد } وهو يوم بدر { لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا } منجى ولا ملجأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʾala means to escape, and waʾala ilayhi means to flee or seek refuge with him.
rows.anchor: يقال : ( وأل ) إذا نجا ، و ( وأل إليه ) إذا لجأ إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns are those of earlier peoples such as Thamūd and Lot’s people, pointed out as a lesson to the Meccans.
rows.anchor: { وتلك القرى } يريد قرى الأولين من ثمود وقوم لوط وغيرهم : أشار لهم إليها ليعتبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Syntactically, ‘those towns’ can be a subject with ‘towns’ as its adjective and ‘We destroyed them’ as predicate; alternatively, it is an object of an implied ‘We destroyed,’ explained by the following clause. It means their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: { تلك } مبتدأ ، و { القرى } صفة : لأن أسماء الإشارة توصف بأسماء الأجناس ، و { أهلكناهم } خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns were destroyed when they acted unjustly, like the Meccans; their destruction had a fixed appointed time that was not delayed, as Mecca’s was Badr.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وتلك أصحاب القرى أهلكناهم { لما ظلموا } مثل ظلم أهل مكة { وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا } وضربنا لإهلاكهم وقتا معلوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahlak is read with an open mīm and either open or closed lām, meaning their destruction or its time; mawʿid can mean a time or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لمهلكهم ) بفتح الميم ، واللام مفتوحة أو مكسورة ، أي : لهلاكهم أو وقت هلاكهم

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: Fatā means servant; a hadith recommends saying ‘my young man/woman’ instead of ‘my male/female slave.’ Joshua son of Nun is identified as Moses’ attendant, called this because he served and followed him; another view says he learned from Moses.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( 643 ) ليقل أحدكم فتاي وفتاتي ، ولا يقل : عبدي وأمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although lā abraḥ can mean ‘I do not leave’ and suggest staying, here it means ‘I will keep going’; its omitted predicate is supplied by the travel context and the goal clause, namely ‘travel until I reach.’
rows.anchor: قلت : هو بمعنى لا أزال ، وقد حذف الخبر ؛ لأن الحال والكلام معا يدلان عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another subtle parse makes ‘my journey will not cease’ the predicate and treats ‘until I reach’ as its subject complement, with an omitted genitive replaced by the first-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر : وهو أن يكون المعنى : لا يبرح مسيري حتى أبلغ على أن حتى أبلغ هو الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses means he will persist in his pursuit and not abandon or leave it until he reaches the meeting place, as one says ‘I will not leave the place.’
rows.anchor: لا أبرح ما أنا عليه ، بمعنى : ألزم المسير والطلب ولا أتركه ولا أفارقه حتى أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting of the two seas is the promised meeting place with al-Khiḍr, where the Persian and Roman seas meet toward the east.
rows.anchor: ومجمع البحرين : المكان الذي وعد فيه موسى لقاء الخضر عليهما السلام ، وهو ملتقى بحري فارس والروم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another identification of the meeting place is Tangier.
rows.anchor: وقيل : طنجة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls it an eccentric interpretation to take the two seas as Moses and al-Khiḍr because they were both seas of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أن البحرين موسى والخضر ، لأنهما كانا بحرين في العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuquban means a long period, defined as eighty years.
rows.anchor: أو أسير زمانا طويلا . والحقب ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and settled with them after Pharaoh’s people perished, he preached God’s favor and his own election and divine speech; when asked who was most learned, he answered ‘I am.’ God reproached him for not referring knowledge to Him and disclosed a more learned servant, al-Khiḍr.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما ظهر موسى على مصر مع بني إسرائيل واستقروا بها بعد هلاك القبط ، أمره الله أن يذكر قومه النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report places al-Khiḍr before Moses, in the days of Afrīdūn, as the vanguard of the greater Dhū al-Qarnayn, and says he lived until Moses’ era.
rows.anchor: وكان الخضر في أيام أفريدون قبل موسى عليه السلام ، وكان على مقدمة ذي القرنين الأكبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Moses asked who was dearest to God; God answered the one who remembers and never forgets Him, then said the most just is one who judges fairly without following desire.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن موسى سأل ربه : أي عبادك أحب إليك ؟ قال الذي يذكرني ولا ينساني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternate explanation for calling Joshua ‘his young man’ is that he learned from Moses.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان يأخذ منه العلم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majmaʿ is also read with a kasra on the mīm, an anomalous pattern like mashriq and maṭliʿ.
rows.anchor: وهي في الشذوذ من يفعل ، كالمشرق والمطلع من يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story says Moses told his attendant to alert him if the fish was lost; while Moses slept the fish jumped into the sea. At breakfast the attendant explained what happened; they returned to the rock, where Moses met a man wrapped in his garment. Al-Khiḍr said each had knowledge from God unavailable to the other; a bird drinking from the sea illustrated how little their knowledge was beside God’s.
rows.anchor: فقال : يا موسى ، أنا على علم علمنيه الله لا تعلمه أنت ، وأنت على علم علمكه الله لا أعلمه أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They forgot their fish’ means they neglected to monitor what happened to it, though it had been made a sign for finding their goal; alternatively, Joshua forgot to present it and Moses forgot to ask about it.
rows.anchor: نسيا حوتهما } أي نسيا تفقد أمره وما يكون منه مما جعل أمارة على الظفر بالطلبة . وقيل : نسي يوشع أن يقدمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the fish was salted; Joshua carried the fish and bread, and after they stopped overnight at the spring of life and Moses slept, the fish revived in the cool, fresh water and fell into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان الحوت سمكة مملوحة . وقيل : إن يوشع حمل الحوت والخبز في المكتل ، فنزلا ليلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other accounts say they ate some of the fish, or that Joshua’s ablution splashed water onto it and revived it before it entered the water.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنهما أكلا منها . وقيل : توضأ يوشع من تلك العين فانتضح الماء على الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saraban means God held back the water’s flow over the fish, making an arch like a vault and a tunnel; this was a miracle for Moses or al-Khiḍr.
rows.anchor: { سربا } أمسك الله جرية الماء على الحوت فصار عليه مثل الطاق ، وحصل منه في مثل السرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They passed the appointed site, the rock, because Moses forgot to watch for the fish’s sign and Joshua forgot to tell him that it had come alive and entered the sea.
rows.anchor: { فلما جاوزا } الموعد وهو الصخرة لنسيان موسى تفقد أمر الحوت وما كان منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say they traveled beyond the rock through the night and until midday; hunger and fatigue struck Moses only after they passed their destination, prompting him to remember and ask for the fish.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سارا بعد مجاوزة الصخرة الليلة والغد إلى الظهر ، وألقى على موسى النصب والجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘This journey’ points to their travel beyond the rock.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { من سفرنا هاذا } إشارة إلى مسيرهما وراء الصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arayta means ‘tell me’; when Moses asked for the fish, Joshua recalled what he had seen and his forgetting, then, astonished, asked Moses about what had happened; some identify this rock as the one below the Oil River.
rows.anchor: لما طلب موسى عليه السلام الحوت ، ذكر يوشع ما رأى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘To remember it’ is an appositive explaining the pronoun in ‘made me forget it’; ʿAbd Allāh’s reading also has ‘that I remember it.’
rows.anchor: و { أن أذكره } بدل من الهاء في { أنسانيه } أي : وما أنساني ذكره إلا الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajaban is the second object of ittakhadha, like saraban: it describes the fish’s extraordinary tunnel-like route; alternatively, it is Joshua or Moses expressing astonishment at the marvel and forgetting.
rows.anchor: و { عجبا } ثاني مفعولي اتخذ ، مثل { سربا } يعني : واتخذ سبيله سبيلا عجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about Satan interruptingly explains the speaker’s forgetting between the coordinated clauses.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وما * أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره } اعتراض بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That is what we were seeking’ points to the fish’s taking its route as a sign of finding al-Khiḍr; fa-rtaddā means they retraced their steps, and qaṣaṣan means following their tracks or retracing them deliberately.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى اتخاذه سبيلا ، أي : ذلك الذي كنا نطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabghi is read without yāʾ in connected recitation, though retaining it is preferable and is Abū ʿAmr’s reading; most omit it at pause in accord with the codex spelling.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( نبغ ) لغير ياء في الوصل ، وإثباتها أحسن ، وهي قراءة أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They returned retracing their tracks; qaṣaṣan means following their tracks or retracing them deliberately.
rows.anchor: فارتدا } فرجعا في أدراجهما { قصصا } يقصان قصصا ، أي : يتبعان آثارهما اتباعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy given to the servant is revelation and prophethood, while the knowledge from God’s presence is knowledge reserved to Him, namely reports of the unseen.
rows.anchor: رحمة من عندنا } هي الوحي والنبوة { من لدنا } مما يختص بنا من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushdan is read with two fatḥas or with ḍamma and sukūn; both mean sound guidance, or knowledge that guides Moses in his religion.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( بفتحتين ) و ( بضمة وسكون ) أي : علما ذا رشد ، أرشد به في ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ need to learn from someone contemporaneous does not imply he was a different Moses, son of Mīshā, rather than Moses son of ʿImrān; a prophet may learn from an equal prophet, though not an inferior.
rows.anchor: قلت : لا غضاضة بالنبي في أخذ العلم من نبي مثله : وإنما بغض منه أن يأخذه ممن دونه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr told Ibn ʿAbbās that Nawf, son of Kaʿb’s wife, claimed al-Khiḍr was not Moses’ companion and this Moses was Moses son of Mīshā; Ibn ʿAbbās called him a liar and enemy of God.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد ابن جبير أنه قال لابن عباس : إن نوفا ابن امرأة كعب يزعم أن الخضر ليس بصاحب موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic denial treats patience as impossible or unworkable, because the guide will do things that appear objectionable; even a righteous person, especially a prophet, cannot help reacting with aversion and objection.
rows.anchor: نفي استطاعة الصبر على وجه التأكيد ، كأنهما مما لا يصح ولا يستقيم ، وعلل ذلك بأنه يتولى أمورا هي في ظاهرها مناكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous person, and especially a prophet, cannot contain disgust, distress, and protest when seeing such actions.
rows.anchor: والرجل الصالح فكيف إذا كان نبيا لا يتمالك أن يشمئز ويمتعض ويجزع إذا رأى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khibran is accusative as specification and means knowledge or information: Moses has not been informed about what he has not comprehended.
rows.anchor: و { خبرا } تمييز ، أي : لم يحط به خبرك بمعنى لم تخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā aʿṣī can be accusative coordinated with ṣābiran, meaning ‘patient and not disobedient,’ or it can be coordinated with ‘you will find me.’
rows.anchor: {ولا أعصي } في محل النصب عطفا على { صابرا } أي : ستجدني صابرا وغير عاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hopes his eagerness for learning will let him remain patient after the truth is explained, and promises patience conditionally on God’s will because he knows the ordeal is difficult.
rows.anchor: رجا موسى عليه السلام لحرصه على العلم وازدياده ، أن يستطيع معه صبرا بعد إفصاح الخضر عن حقيقة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reformer’s zeal when seeing wrongdoing is nearly unbearable; although Moses knew the divinely protected prophet he followed was free of religious fault and that apparently ugly actions had a beautiful hidden reason, not knowing that reason makes patience harder.
rows.anchor: وإن الحمية التي تأخذ المصلح عند مشاهدة الفساد شيء لا يطاق ، هذا مع علمه أن النبي المعصوم
